one_line: Paramara king of Malwa who restored stability after Bhoja and used temples and inscriptions to uphold his dynasty.

appearance.age_look: early 40s, medium-tall, solid but not bulky build with a dignified warrior-king presence
appearance.face: oval face, medium-brown Malwa complexion, sharp straight nose, neatly trimmed medium-length beard and moustache, arched brows over large intense anime-style eyes, default expression calm and thoughtful with a hint of determined steel
appearance.hair: thick black hair pulled back into a high, neat knot at the back of the crown, wrapped with a narrow gold cloth band; no crown, but a simple thin gold circlet resting low on the forehead with a tiny central red stone
appearance.costume: era-accurate 11th-century Paramara royal attire: a long-sleeved, thigh-length angarakha-style tunic of rich deep maroon silk with subtle gold woven borders, worn wrapped left-over-right and tied with an embroidered golden-yellow cloth belt; below it a full, ankle-length off-white cotton dhoti, pleated in front and wrapped securely, with a thin maroon border; over one shoulder a lightweight pale-cream uttariya (shawl) with fine red and gold stripes at the edges, draped from the left shoulder diagonally across the torso and wrapped around the right forearm; on the chest, a flat, broad gold necklace with simple round pendants, paired with two slimmer chains; gold kadas (bracelets) on both wrists and a narrow armlet on the right upper arm; small round gold earrings; feet in brown leather strapped sandals; textiles look real and slightly worn at edges, suited for a ruler who moves between court and temple sites rather than ceremonial excess.
appearance.signature: A rolled copperplate charter held in his left hand, wrapped with a red cord and sealed with a visible circular copper seal, symbolising his temple grants and prashasti inscriptions.

ref_desc: Udayaditya is a medium-tall, early-40s Malwa king with a medium-brown oval face, black hair in a high knot with a thin gold circlet, wearing a deep maroon angarakha, off-white dhoti, cream uttariya, gold jewellery, brown sandals, and holding a red-tied rolled copperplate charter.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Udayaditya of Malwa: a medium-tall, early-40s Paramara king with a medium-brown oval face, large serious eyes, straight nose, and a neatly trimmed beard and moustache, his thick black hair pulled into a high knot wrapped with a narrow gold cloth band and a thin gold circlet with a tiny red stone resting low on his forehead; dress him in an 11th-century central Indian royal outfit consisting of a long-sleeved, thigh-length deep maroon silk angarakha-wrapped tunic with subtle gold borders, tied at the waist by an embroidered golden-yellow cloth belt, over a full ankle-length off-white cotton dhoti with a thin maroon border, and drape a pale-cream uttariya with fine red and gold edge stripes from his left shoulder across his chest and around his right forearm; add a broad flat gold necklace with small round pendants, two slimmer gold chains, gold bracelets on both wrists, a narrow upper armlet on the right arm, and small round gold earrings, and put brown leather strapped sandals on his feet; in his left hand place a rolled copperplate charter bound with a red cord and a visible circular copper seal, while his right hand rests relaxed at his side or lightly on his belt; use a palette of deep maroon, golden yellow, off-white, pale cream, and brown leather, and present him in neutral, well-lit poses from front, side, and back views to clearly show hair, costume, and the copperplate charter as his constant signature prop.
